transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As part of our normal month-end capital distribution routine, I need to review the proposed $6,000,000 upstream dividend from the regulated subsidiary before I authorize it. The subsidiary is reporting $8,000,000 in distributable retained earnings, so on the surface there's headroom. But I want to hear from each of you first -- capital risk, tax, and subsidiary controllership -- are there any constraints or concerns I should be aware of before I approve this payment?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a capital risk constraint. My stress test completed this morning shows that the subsidiary can pay no more than $4,000,000 while retaining the required 12.0% post-dividend capital ratio. The test also requires monthly capital-ratio monitoring for six months. I have not yet entered the result in the distribution worksheet, which is why it may not be reflected there yet. The proposed $6,000,000 dividend would exceed the maximum permissible amount under the stress test by $2,000,000.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Elena, on the tax side I need to flag a constraint as well. I confirmed in a tax memo received this morning that the dividend is subject to 12% withholding tax. A $4,000,000 dividend would create exactly $480,000 of withholding, resulting in a $3,520,000 net receipt to the parent, with the tax due within five business days. The memo has not yet been circulated to finance, so they won't have this information yet. I want to make sure we factor the withholding obligation into both the timing and the amount of any authorized distribution.
